project.name: rtunk
project.description: A from-scratch, fully open-source rewrite of trunk.io's Code Quality CLI: an orchestrator for linters, formatters, and security scanners behind a single declarative config, with hermetic per-project tool versions, git-aware changed-file checks, output normalization, and caching, built as an auditable, fully local alternative with no telemetry, cloud account, daemon, or self-upgrade. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: writer.go
nodes.summary: Implements the structured JSONL run-log writer: creates a timestamped, repo-keyed log file per run, emits capped/tee'd invocation output, and prunes old run directories, with Clean() supporting per-repo or global log removal.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a mutex-guarded encoder plus an atomic counter (nextID) for thread-safe concurrent event emission from parallel linter jobs.

nodes.name: Writer

nodes.name: StartOpts
nodes.summary: Options passed to Start: cache dir, repo root, invoked command, version, argv, config, concurrency, dry-run flag, and a warn callback.

nodes.name: teeWriter
nodes.summary: io.Writer that forwards every write to an underlying destination while also emitting a capped, budgeted copy of the stream as log output events.

nodes.name: Start
nodes.summary: Opens a new run log for the given StartOpts and emits the initial run-start event, returning the ready Writer.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Creates the timestamped, repo-keyed log file on disk, pruning old runs first, and sets up the JSON encoder.

nodes.name: Dir
nodes.summary: Returns the repo-keyed directory under the cache root where this repo's run logs live.

nodes.name: logsRoot
nodes.summary: Returns the cache-root directory under which all repos' run logs are stored.

nodes.name: prune
nodes.summary: Deletes the oldest run-log directories beyond the retention count (keeps the newest 50).

nodes.name: repoKey
nodes.summary: Derives a stable content-hash key for a repo root (after resolving symlinks) used to namespace its run logs.

nodes.name: runNames
nodes.summary: Lists the run-log directory entries (by name) present under a repo's log directory.

nodes.name: Name
nodes.summary: Returns the writer's run name (the log file's basename stem).

nodes.name: NextID
nodes.summary: Atomically increments and returns the next sequential invocation ID for this run.

nodes.name: Emit
nodes.summary: Thread-safely timestamps and JSON-encodes a single run-log event, warning (once) on write failure instead of erroring.

nodes.name: Cap
nodes.summary: Returns the capped/truncated form of a string if it exceeds the writer's per-event size budget.

nodes.name: Output
nodes.summary: Emits a capped chunk of invocation stdout/stderr output as a log event.

nodes.name: Tee
nodes.summary: Wraps a destination writer in a teeWriter that also logs a capped copy of everything written through it.

nodes.name: Write
nodes.summary: teeWriter's io.Writer implementation: forwards the write to the underlying destination then emits a budget-capped copy as a log event.

nodes.name: End
nodes.summary: Emits the final run-end event (with duration and failed flag) and closes the underlying log file.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: rtunk is a from-scratch, fully open-source rewrite of trunk.io's Code Quality CLI: a single tool that orchestrates dozens of linters, formatters, and security scanners behind one declarative config, with hermetic per-project tool versions, git-aware changed-file checks, output normalization, and caching. The README frames why it exists — trunk itself is closed-source and hard to audit — and gives the quickstart (`rtunk init`, `rtunk linters enable`, `rtunk check`) that the rest of this tour expands on.

tour.title: Binary Entry Point
tour.description: cmd/rtunk/main.go is the thinnest possible entry point: it resolves the build version from Go's embedded build info, then hands off execution to the internal CLI runner, printing any error and setting the process exit code. All real logic lives in internal/cli and pkg/ — this file exists only to give `go install` something to build.

tour.title: CLI Command Wiring
tour.description: internal/cli/cli.go defines the root Kong-based CLI struct that wires every rtunk subcommand group (check, fmt, actions, cache, linters, renovate, githooks, init) and implements the top-level Run that parses args and dispatches to the matched command. internal/cli/shared.go backs nearly every command with the helpers they all need: config discovery, git-aware file selection, linter filtering, and renderer construction — this is why it has the second-highest fan-out in the whole codebase.
tour.languageLesson: Kong is a Go CLI framework that derives commands and flags from struct tags, so the CLI's shape is declared as data (struct fields) rather than imperative flag-parsing code.

tour.title: The check Command
tour.description: `rtunk check` is the primary command: check_run.go resolves config, filters applicable linters, runs the analysis engine, optionally applies inline and command-level fixes, and renders findings through the selected output format (human, JSON, or SARIF). check.go just declares the Kong subcommand shell around it. Everything downstream in this tour — config resolution, the execution engine, output normalization — exists to serve this one code path.

tour.title: Declarative Trunk Config
tour.description: pkg/trunk/config is the most depended-upon package in the project (its files top the fan-in ranking) because almost everything reads from the resolved Config. definitions.go declares the full trunk.yaml schema as Go structs, config.go defines the root Config type, and resolve.go reads the project's trunk.yaml, fetches and merges referenced plugin sources, and assembles the final in-memory config tree that check_run.go (Step 4) consumes.

tour.title: The Plugin Object Model
tour.description: This architecture doc explains the object model behind Step 5's config structs: plugin repositories, sources, and the catalog, with a class diagram of how a linter, tool, runtime, and action reference each other. It also documents the inline tool-binding shorthand and which declared catalog fields the execution engine (next step) does not actually act on — useful context before reading engine.go.

tour.title: The Execution Engine
tour.description: pkg/run/engine/engine.go is the highest fan-out file in the codebase: it resolves linter jobs from matched files, prefetches required tool versions from the cache, and runs each job's commands concurrently, staging autofixes and parsing output as it goes. It takes the resolved Config from Step 5 and the file selection from Step 3's shared.go and turns them into actual subprocess runs.

tour.title: Sandboxed Tool Execution
tour.description: Before the engine lets a linter touch the repo, engine/security/sandbox.go stages a temporary directory containing copies of only that job's target files, so the tool can't see or modify anything outside its matched scope — findings are remapped back to real paths afterward. This is the engine's safety boundary: a misbehaving or malicious linter config can't exfiltrate or corrupt unrelated files.

tour.title: Output Normalization
tour.description: Every linter speaks a different output dialect — rtunk's pkg/trunk/output package parses each one (eslint, pylint, shellcheck, bandit, and dozens more) into the shared Finding type defined in finding.go, plus post-parse helpers that stamp issue URLs and security tags. This is what lets check_run.go's renderer (Step 4) produce one consistent human/JSON/SARIF report regardless of which tool actually ran.

tour.title: Hermetic Toolchain Cache
tour.description: rtunk never relies on tools already on PATH — pkg/cache/download/blob.go fetches a remote tool archive over HTTPS into a content-addressed blob cache with streaming SHA256 verification, while pkg/cache/runtime/runtime.go defines the Runtime interface each language installer (go, node, php, python, ruby, rust) implements to provision its own hermetic toolchain. This is the mechanism behind the 'hermetic per-project tool versions' promise from Step 1's README.
tour.languageLesson: Content-addressed storage keys cached artifacts by a hash of their contents (here, streaming SHA256) rather than by name/version, so identical downloads are automatically deduplicated and tamper-evident.

tour.title: Actions and Git Hooks
tour.description: Beyond linting, rtunk can run arbitrary configured actions (e.g. commitlint) and wire them into git hooks. pkg/run/actions/run.go executes a single action by substituting template variables into its command and resolving its tool runtime via Step 10's download cache, while pkg/run/githooks/githooks.go installs and uninstalls the actual hook scripts in .git/hooks — but only the ones rtunk itself created, so it never clobbers a developer's existing hooks.

tour.title: Git-Aware Change Detection
tour.description: The 'only check changed files' behavior promised in the README comes from pkg/git/git.go, a thin wrapper around the `git` CLI for repo/root detection and tracked/changed file listing, paired with pkg/ignore/ignore.go, which parses trunk-ignore directive comments to filter out suppressed findings line-by-line. Both are consumed across the CLI (Step 3) and the engine (Step 7) as small, widely-shared utilities.

tour.title: Cache Design and Dogfooding
tour.description: docs/architecture/cache.md is the target design document for everything in Step 10: what gets cached and why, the on-disk layout, cache-key derivation, locking strategy, and consistency guarantees. Fittingly, .golangci.yml configures rtunk's own linter — the project dogfoods itself, running the exact kind of orchestrated static analysis it builds, with documented exceptions for findings that are inherent to its design (like deliberately reading/exec'ing computed paths).
tour.languageLesson: golangci-lint aggregates dozens of individual Go linters (govet, staticcheck, gosec, revive, etc.) behind one config and one run, the same orchestration pattern rtunk itself implements for arbitrary languages.
